name: Manipulonyx
sum: Small parvicursorine alvarezsaurid from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of Mongolia, with the most complete forelimb known for its subfamily.
wsnote: No body size given in the sources consulted.
holotype: PIN 3142/364, a partial skeleton (cervical, dorsal, sacral and caudal vertebrae, left scapulocoracoid, most of both forelimbs, partial pelvis, hindlimb fragments), Khermeen Tsav, Nemegt Formation, Mongolia.
material: Only the holotype, found in 1979 by V. Yu. Reshetov.
biology: Like other alvarezsaurids it had a one-fingered hand with an enlarged claw, plus ossified spikes on the wrist that the describers interpret as an adaptation for eating eggs; slender hindlimbs suggest running.
author: Averianov, Lopatin & Atuchin 2025

sources.text: Alexander O. Averianov, Alexey V. Lopatin, Andrey A. Atuchin 2025. Forelimb structure and function in a new Late Cretaceous parvicursorine theropod dinosaur from Mongolia. Proceedings of the Zoological Institute RAS. doi:10.31610/trudyzin/2025.329.4.382

dates_note: No PBDB record. Nemegt Formation is Maastrichtian (Wikipedia revision 1387598631); ICS bounds of the stage used.
